title: Fine fans, their saturated ideal blowups and smooth functorial towers
statement:
Write commutative monoids additively, with identity $0$. Use group completion as in [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. A monoid $P$ is fine if it is finitely generated and its map to $P^{\mathrm{gp}}$ is injective; sharp if its only unit is $0$; and saturated if $ng\in P$, $g\in P^{\mathrm{gp}}$, $n>0$ implies $g\in P$. For an integral monoid and a submonoid $S$, localization means $P-S=\{p-s:p\in P,s\in S\}\subset P^{\mathrm{gp}}$; write $P[a^{-1}]=P-\mathbf N a$. Its saturation is $P^{\mathrm{sat}}=\{g\in P^{\mathrm{gp}}:ng\in P\text{ for some integer }n>0\}$. For any monoid $Q$, put $Q^\times=\{u\in Q:\exists v\in Q,\ u+v=0\}$; its sharpening $\overline Q=Q/Q^\times$ identifies elements differing by addition of a unit.

An ideal $I\subset P$ is a subset with $I+P\subset I$; it is prime if it is proper and $P\setminus I$ is closed under addition. The monoid spectrum $\operatorname{Spec}_{\mathrm{mon}}P$ is the set of prime ideals, including the empty ideal, with basic opens $D(a)=\{\mathfrak p:a\notin\mathfrak p\}$. Its monoid sheaf $\widetilde P$ has sections $P[a^{-1}]$ on $D(a)$ and the localization restriction maps. Here a sheaf of monoids means a presheaf of commutative monoids whose underlying presheaf of sets is a sheaf [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, clause (1)], on the site of open subsets with inclusions and open covers. A stalk consists of germs $(U,s)$ modulo equality after restriction to a smaller neighborhood. The sharp sheaf $\overline{\widetilde P}$ is the sheafification of $U\mapsto\widetilde P(U)/\widetilde P(U)^\times$ [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], with addition induced locally from addition of representatives.

A fine fan $(F,\mathcal P_F)$ is a topological space with a sheaf of sharp monoids locally isomorphic to $(\operatorname{Spec}_{\mathrm{mon}}P,\overline{\widetilde P})$ for fine $P$; these local models are its affine charts. A morphism $f:(G,\mathcal P_G)\to(F,\mathcal P_F)$ consists of a continuous map and homomorphisms $\mathcal P_F(U)\to\mathcal P_G(f^{-1}U)$ compatible with restrictions, such that the induced homomorphisms on stalks are local. A homomorphism $h:P\to Q$ is local if $h^{-1}(Q^\times)=P^\times$. The fan is torsion free if every group $\mathcal P_{F,z}^{\mathrm{gp}}$ has $ng=0$, $n>0$, only for $g=0$; saturated if every stalk is saturated; and smooth if every stalk is isomorphic to $\mathbf N^r$ for some finite $r\geq0$. A fan morphism is smooth if every stalk map identifies with the inclusion $P\to P\oplus\mathbf N^r$ for some finite $r\geq0$.

A nonempty coherent ideal $J\subset\mathcal P_F$ is a subsheaf stable under addition by $\mathcal P_F$, locally generated as an ideal by a finite nonempty set of sections. Pullback of an ideal is the ideal generated by its image. On an affine chart for a sharp fine monoid $P$, with ideal $I$ generated by a finite nonempty set $E$, put $Q_a=\langle P,b-a\ (b\in E)\rangle\subset P^{\mathrm{gp}}$ and $C_a=Q_a^{\mathrm{sat}}$, for $a\in E$. Equivalently $Q_a$ is generated by $P$ and all $b-a$ with $b\in I$. The saturated blowup has affine charts $(\operatorname{Spec}_{\mathrm{mon}}C_a,\overline{\widetilde C_a})$. The fineness of $C_a$ and compatibility of saturation with localization are supplied by [lem-trf-fine-monoid-finite-saturation]; the fine saturated sharp quotients used in their stalks are supplied by [lem-trf-fs-face-sharpening]. For $a,b\in E$, glue the $a$-chart on $D(b-a)$ to the $b$-chart on $D(a-b)$ using the identity of their localized monoids inside $P^{\mathrm{gp}}$. These prescriptions are used on affine charts of $F$ and glued on restrictions. Gluing means the quotient of the disjoint union by these open identifications, with sections the tuples of local sections agreeing on identified overlaps.

A finite saturated blowup tower is a finite sequence $F_n\to\cdots\to F_0$, together with its ordered ideal centers; $n=0$ is allowed. Its pullback along $G\to F_0$ is defined recursively, starting with $G$, by saturated blowup along the pulled-back center at each stage. Contraction deletes the stages whose center is the whole monoid sheaf and whose morphism is an isomorphism; a nontrivial saturation of a nonsaturated fan is retained even if its center is the whole monoid sheaf. A smooth-functorial saturated desingularization assigns to every fine torsion-free fan with a finite affine cover a finite saturated blowup tower with smooth last fan. For each smooth morphism $g:G\to F$, its assigned tower on $G$ is canonically identified with the contracted pullback of the assigned tower on $F$, retaining the centers and their order, with these identifications compatible with identity morphisms and composition.

split_report.summary: Repair of D1/B4: withdrew all three redundant, unmerged definition children. All TeX is written as raw strings and checked after JSON decoding. Clarified contraction to retain a nonidentity initial saturation: the unit center alone does not make a saturated blowup an isomorphism on a nonsaturated fan. No new nodes and no Lean work.
